title: Esther 4: Mordecai Charges Esther for Such a Time as This
body:
Read the chapter → [Esther 4](/bible/esther/4)

**[Esther 4:1-3](/bible/esther/4#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/esther/4#v1)</sup> When Mordecai perceived all that was done, Mordecai rent his clothes, and put on sackcloth with ashes, and went out into the midst of the city, and cried with a loud and a bitter cry;
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/esther/4#v2)</sup> And came even before the king’s gate: for none might enter into the king’s gate clothed with sackcloth.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/esther/4#v3)</sup> And in every province, whithersoever the king’s commandment and his decree came, there was great mourning among the Jews, and fasting, and weeping, and wailing; and many lay in sackcloth and ashes.

- When Mordecai perceived all that was done he rent his clothes, put on sackcloth with ashes, went out into the midst of the city and cried with a loud and bitter cry, and came before the king's gate, for none might enter it clothed with sackcloth.
- In every province where the king's commandment and decree came there was great mourning among the Jews, with fasting, weeping and wailing, and many lay in sackcloth and ashes. Imagine a decree today to kill every descendant of Israel, and you begin to feel what they went through.

**[Esther 4:4-9](/bible/esther/4#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/esther/4#v4)</sup> So Esther’s maids and her chamberlains came and told it her. Then was the queen exceedingly grieved; and she sent raiment to clothe Mordecai, and to take away his sackcloth from him: but he received it not.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/esther/4#v5)</sup> Then called Esther for Hatach, one of the king’s chamberlains, whom he had appointed to attend upon her, and gave him a commandment to Mordecai, to know what it was, and why it was.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/esther/4#v6)</sup> So Hatach went forth to Mordecai unto the street of the city, which was before the king’s gate.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/esther/4#v7)</sup> And Mordecai told him of all that had happened unto him, and of the sum of the money that Haman had promised to pay to the king’s treasuries for the Jews, to destroy them.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/esther/4#v8)</sup> Also he gave him the copy of the writing of the decree that was given at Shushan to destroy them, to shew it unto Esther, and to declare it unto her, and to charge her that she should go in unto the king, to make supplication unto him, and to make request before him for her people.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/esther/4#v9)</sup> And Hatach came and told Esther the words of Mordecai.

- Esther's maids and chamberlain told her, and the queen was exceedingly grieved and sent raiment to clothe Mordecai and take away his sackcloth, but he received it not. She sent Hatach, appointed to attend her, to learn what it was and why.
- Mordecai told Hatach all that had happened and of the money Haman promised to pay for the Jews to be destroyed, and gave him a copy of the decree published in Shushan to show Esther, charging her to go in to the king and make supplication for her people.

**[Esther 4:10-12](/bible/esther/4#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/esther/4#v10)</sup> Again Esther spake unto Hatach, and gave him commandment unto Mordecai;
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/esther/4#v11)</sup> All the king’s servants, and the people of the king’s provinces, do know, that whosoever, whether man or woman, shall come unto the king into the inner court, who is not called, there is one law of his to put him to death, except such to whom the king shall hold out the golden sceptre, that he may live: but I have not been called to come in unto the king these thirty days.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/esther/4#v12)</sup> And they told to Mordecai Esther’s words.

- Esther answered by Hatach that all the king's servants and people knew that whosoever came unto the king in the inner court uncalled, man or woman, there was one law, to be put to death, except the king held out the golden sceptre that he may live.
- She said she had not been called to come in unto the king these thirty days, and they told Mordecai her words. She made an excuse, though she was the queen the king had chosen and loved above all the women.

**[Esther 4:13-14](/bible/esther/4#v13)**

> <sup>[13](/bible/esther/4#v13)</sup> Then Mordecai commanded to answer Esther, Think not with thyself that thou shalt escape in the king’s house, more than all the Jews.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/esther/4#v14)</sup> For if thou altogether holdest thy peace at this time, then shall there enlargement and deliverance arise to the Jews from another place; but thou and thy father’s house shall be destroyed: and who knoweth whether thou art come to the kingdom for such a time as this?

- Mordecai sent answer that Esther should not think she would escape in the king's house more than all the Jews, for if she altogether held her peace at this time, then enlargement and deliverance would arise to the Jews from another place, but she and her father's house would be destroyed.
- Who knoweth whether Esther was come to the kingdom for such a time as this. She was put in her position to serve this very purpose, and the deliverance of Israel cannot be held back; she would either help it along or be left behind while it came another way.

**[Esther 4:15-17](/bible/esther/4#v15)**

> <sup>[15](/bible/esther/4#v15)</sup> Then Esther bade them return Mordecai this answer,
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/esther/4#v16)</sup> Go, gather together all the Jews that are present in Shushan, and fast ye for me, and neither eat nor drink three days, night or day: I also and my maidens will fast likewise; and so will I go in unto the king, which is not according to the law: and if I perish, I perish.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/esther/4#v17)</sup> So Mordecai went his way, and did according to all that Esther had commanded him.

- Esther returned answer that Mordecai should gather all the Jews in Shushan to fast for her, neither eating nor drinking three days, night or day, and she and her maidens would fast likewise, and so she would go in unto the king not according to the law, and if she perished, she perished.
- So Mordecai went his way and did according to all Esther commanded him. She had her mind set right, ready to risk her life for her people.

  - **[1 Esdras 4:28-31](/bible/1-esdras/4#v28)**
    > <sup>[28](/bible/1-esdras/4#v28)</sup> And now do ye not believe me? is not the king great in his power? do not all regions fear to touch him?
    >
    > <sup>[29](/bible/1-esdras/4#v29)</sup> Yet did I see him and Apame the king’s concubine, the daughter of the admirable Bartacus, sitting at the right hand of the king,
    >
    > <sup>[30](/bible/1-esdras/4#v30)</sup> And taking the crown from the king’s head, and setting it upon her own head; she also struck the king with her left hand.
    >
    > <sup>[31](/bible/1-esdras/4#v31)</sup> And yet for all this the king gaped and gazed upon her with open mouth: if she laughed upon him, he laughed also: but if she took any displeasure at him, the king was fain to flatter, that she might be reconciled to him again.

    Zerubbabel's wisdom before the king shows that a woman holds power over even the great king, so Esther should not fear to use the influence she has.

  - **[Romans 15:4](/bible/romans/15#v4)**
    > <sup>[4](/bible/romans/15#v4)</sup> For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.

    The things written beforetime were written for our learning, which is why Mordecai would not accept a weak answer from Esther but held her to her purpose.
